steps.explanationAfterStep: Protonation gives the tertiary cation. This slow step sets the regiochemistry: OH will end up on the more substituted carbon (Markovnikov).
Water is a weak nucleophile, but the cation is very reactive. The oxygen is now positively charged.
Water takes the proton: tert-butanol, and H₃O⁺ is regenerated. Every step is reversible: concentrated acid and heat run it backwards (E1 dehydration).

title: Hydration of 2-methylpropene
subtitle: Acid-catalysed addition of water
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 20

cation.caption: tert-butyl cation + water
hintTiers: What is the nucleophile in the flask, and where is the positive charge?
A water oxygen gives a lone pair to the cationic carbon. One arrow.
From a lone pair on a water oxygen to the positively charged carbon.
cation.learnerPrompt: The tertiary cation meets water. Draw the next step.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Taking that proton back gives the alkene again: the reverse of the step you just drew. Water adds to the cation here.

oxonium.caption: protonated tert-butanol (an oxonium ion) + water
hintTiers: The oxygen carries a positive charge and two H atoms. What can remove one of them?
Another water molecule takes a proton from the oxonium oxygen; the O–H bond breaks onto that oxygen. Two arrows.
Arrow 1: from a lone pair of a free water to an H on the oxonium oxygen. Arrow 2: from that O–H bond onto the oxonium oxygen.
oxonium.learnerPrompt: Turn the oxonium ion into the neutral alcohol.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Losing water gives back the tert-butyl cation: the reverse of the last step. Remove a proton instead.

reactants.caption: 2-methylpropene + H₃O⁺ (hydrogen sulfate counter-ion) + water
hintTiers: Which species is the strongest acid here? What does the alkene π bond do to it?
The π bond takes a proton from H₃O⁺, and the O–H bond breaks onto oxygen. Put the H where the cation left behind is most substituted. Two arrows.
Arrow 1: from the C=C π bond to the H of H₃O⁺, forming a bond from the CH₂ carbon to H. Arrow 2: from that O–H bond onto the oxygen.
reactants.learnerPrompt: Dilute acid adds water across the C=C bond. Draw the first step.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: That leaves a primary cation on the CH₂ carbon. Put the proton on the CH₂ carbon instead: the positive charge then sits on the tertiary carbon, stabilised by three methyl groups.
Water cannot attack an alkene: both are nucleophiles. The alkene must first be protonated.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right start. Hydrogen can only have one bond: break the O–H bond of H₃O⁺ onto oxygen.

mechanismSummary: H₃O⁺ protonates the CH₂ end of the alkene, giving the tertiary tert-butyl cation. Water adds to the cation, and a second water takes a proton from the oxonium ion. The product is tert-butanol, and H₃O⁺ is given back: the acid is a catalyst.
